label: Fig 1
title: Precision-recall curves among unlabeled test students.
caption: Panel A shows HGB procedures and Panel B shows logistic procedures and the added EM estimators for the fixed seed 42 baseline cohort. Both recall and precision are calculated within U, the test students with S = 0. The dotted horizontal line marks the realized hardship prevalence within this unlabeled test population. Legend values report AP_U for this cohort. Models trained on true hardship labels are learner-specific references. This fixed-seed illustration is distinct from the aggregate comparison across 100 cohorts in Table 1; it does not establish the representativeness of any single cohort.

label: Fig 2
title: Screening capacity and yield among unlabeled test students.
caption: Curves show cohort means for the HGB procedures and the low-spending baseline across 100 baseline cohorts. Capacity ranges from 1% to 30% of U. Panel A reports hidden-positive recall, the fraction of true positives in U recovered by the shortlist; shading shows pointwise 95% cohort bootstrap intervals. Panel B reports precision, the fraction of shortlisted students with true hardship, and displays means without uncertainty bands. Previously recorded positives do not occupy shortlist places. The complete comparison of methods and fixed capacities is reported in Table 1.

label: Fig 3
title: Paired Spy HGB differences across labeling mechanisms.
caption: Points show the mean within-cohort difference between Spy HGB and naive HGB under eight specified labeling mechanisms. Panel A reports AP_full over the entire test population. Panel B reports hidden-positive recall at a capacity of 10% of U. Each mechanism uses 100 matched cohorts, with both methods evaluated on the same training and test split within each cohort. Error bars are unadjusted percentile 95% bootstrap intervals from 10,000 resamples of cohort-level differences. The vertical reference line marks zero difference; positive values favor Spy HGB. The constant-labeling setting is the same cached zero-slope setting used in Fig 7A-B.

label: Fig 4
title: Paired comparisons with naive logistic regression across labeling mechanisms.
caption: Points show mean within-cohort differences for Spy logistic regression, SAR-EM, Index-EM, and LBE-LF relative to naive logistic regression. Panel A reports AP_U and Panel B reports hidden-positive recall at a capacity of 10% of U. Each of the eight mechanisms uses 100 matched cohorts. Error bars are unadjusted percentile 95% bootstrap intervals from 10,000 cohort resamples. The vertical reference line marks zero difference; positive values favor the named method. Index-EM is the restricted-index adaptation specified in Methods, while LBE-LF is a distinct linear implementation of labeling bias estimation.

label: Fig 5
title: Paired Spy HGB differences under stress settings.
caption: Points show the mean within-cohort difference in average precision among unlabeled test students (AP_U), calculated as Spy HGB minus naive HGB. Error bars are unadjusted 95% percentile bootstrap intervals from 10,000 cohort resamples. All ten stress settings (50 matched cohorts each) and the alternative generator (100 matched cohorts) are retained. Positive values favor Spy HGB; negative values favor naive HGB. False-positive record probabilities are conditional on Y = 0. This within-learner comparison does not rank Spy against the EM or LBE-LF estimators.

label: Fig 6
title: Simulator-assisted diagnostics of propensity denominators, calibration, and output clipping.
caption: Each row compares division by the individual latent labeling probability q_tau (circles; abbreviated q in the figure) with division by the conditional propensity e(X) (squares), defined as E[q_tau | X, Y = 1]. Points show mean AP_full over 100 baseline cohorts; error bars are 95% cohort bootstrap intervals. Thin gray segments connect the two denominator choices within the same numerator configuration; they do not represent confidence intervals for their difference. Each denominator is evaluated for every test observation without selection according to its true class. Raw fitted numerators use the full training set; calibrated numerators use an 80% training subset for fitting and the remaining 20% for Platt calibration. Their comparison therefore also changes the training allocation. The capped configuration limits the divided score to one. Known population numerators and conditional propensities are simulator-assisted references unavailable to practical learners. These are diagnostic comparisons, not additional deployable methods or a proof of identification.

label: Fig 7
title: Sensitivity to the inverse-labeling slope.
caption: Points show mean hidden-positive recall at capacities of 5% (A) and 10% (B) of U for the HGB procedures, using 100 cohorts per slope. Error bars are pointwise 95% cohort bootstrap intervals. The labeling-rule intercept is 0.55 + 0.55 times the slope, with bounds of 0.10 and 0.92. The zero-slope setting is the constant-labeling scenario. The slope-0.62 setting differs from the main baseline, which uses intercept 0.88 and bounds of 0.12 and 0.88. Elkan-Noto denotes the weighted HGB procedure.

label: Fig 8
title: Sampling-design simulation for prospective verification of screening recall.
caption: The design verifies all students shortlisted by Spy HGB at a capacity of 10% of U and a simple random sample without replacement of 50, 100, 200, or 400 nonselected students. Each of 100 baseline cohorts contributes 1,000 sampling draws per sample size. Panel A shows the cohort mean exact hypergeometric probability of finding no missed positive in the nonselected sample. Panel B shows the mean cohort-specific root mean squared error of the weighted recall ratio estimator across the 1,000 draws. Missed cases receive inverse-inclusion-probability weights. Error bars are 95% cohort bootstrap intervals. The simulation assumes complete participation and correct verification; it is not an audit of real students. Observing no missed case does not establish complete recall.
